claim: it is unknown whether a person under 20 can pass the disease to an older adult.
justification: The high-confidence evidence from the knowledge-only reasoner (confidence 0.85) states that as of August 2020, the CDC's guidance indicated children could spread COVID-19 to older adults, albeit with lower efficiency and a need for further research. This directly addresses the claim date and demonstrates that transmission from individuals under 20 to older adults was not considered unknown at that time, as authorities acknowledged it as a possibility. Although some evidence from the retrieval-based fact-checker highlights uncertainty in October 2020, the corroborated CDC guidance from August 2020 refutes the claim that it was unknown.
